default.tests.0.skills.2.sections.0.passages.0.s: To start or launch something (a service, activity).
A little while ago, the library in my town started a "digital library service".
a little while ago, a short time ago
Not ~ / Instead of ~ (negates the preceding part to emphasize what follows).
Can do ~, to be able to do ~ (expresses ability or possibility to perform an action).
To come to be able to do ~, to reach the point where ~ (indicates a change from being unable to being able to do something).
Instead of paper books, it has now become possible to borrow and read digital books using computers, smartphones, etc.
Because of that / Therefore / And so (conjunction indicating cause and effect).
Expresses a habit or repeated action regularly performed in the present.
Because of that, recently I have often been using the digital library.
Potential form of Group 2 verbs (借りる → 借りられる: can borrow).
At the digital library, you can borrow books anytime, 24 hours a day.
Can / To be able to do something.
If the book you borrowed is not interesting, you can return it right away and borrow another book.
if not interesting, if not fun
Even if ~ / Even though ~ (何もしなくても: even without doing anything).
Because ~ / Since ~ (indicates an objective cause or reason).
Never ~ / There is no instance of ~ happening.
Also, after two weeks have passed, books are returned without you having to do anything, so you will never be late returning them.
to be late, to be delayed
Because ~ / Since ~ (忙しくて: being busy, so...).
For ~ / To ~ (indicates the target audience or standard of evaluation).
Although the books you can borrow from digital libraries are still few, they are very convenient for people who are too busy to go to the library.
can borrow, to be able to borrow
By / Via / Using (indicates means or method: インターネットで).
And / Such as (used for non-exhaustive listing of nouns).
Can / To be able to do something.
(Note) A library where you can read books, magazines, and newspapers over the Internet.
default.tests.0.skills.2.sections.0.passages.1.s: Nominalizes an action (the act of doing something is...)
Singing karaoke with friends is very fun, but I sometimes go to karaoke alone.
When, at the time of (indicates the timing of an action)
Only... (used with a negative verb to emphasize an exclusive limit)
Potential form of verbs (can / cannot do something)
When singing with friends, I only sing songs that I can sing well; but when I am alone, I often sing new songs or songs that I cannot sing well.
Passive form (to be heard by someone)
Because, since (indicates an objective, polite cause or reason)
Since no one can hear me, I don't feel embarrassed at all.
by anyone, to anyone (with negative verb: by/to no one)
Even if, no matter if (concessive conditional expressing that doing something is fine)
From... (indicates the starting point of an action)
No matter how many times I sing the same song, or if I stop halfway and sing from the beginning, nobody gets angry.
does not get angry, will not get mad
To come to be able to do something (expresses a change in ability or state over time)
In order to, for the purpose of (indicates the goal of an action)
To think that... (expresses personal thoughts or opinions)
I think it is a good way to become able to sing well.
default.tests.0.skills.2.sections.0.passages.2.s: Expresses the existence of an inanimate object at a location (there is something at a place).
There is this note on Mr. Yamamoto's desk.
to exist, to have, there is (inanimate)
Indicates the starting point of an action or the source of information (from someone).
There was a phone call from Mr. Kobayashi of Nakamura Elementary School.
Introduces a topic or states a conditional assumption (if it is...).
Conveys hearsay or secondhand information (I heard that..., it is said that...).
Apparently, the exchange meeting in March can be held at 11:00 or 13:00 on the 3rd (Fri), and at 13:00 on the 23rd (Thu).
can be held, to be possible
After / when... (expresses a subsequent action once a condition is fulfilled).
Expressing a desire to have something (wanting to receive a call).
Reporting what a third party said (said that...).
He said that once the date and time to attend the exchange meeting are decided, he would like a phone call.
can go, to be able to go
once decided, when settled, if decided
Embedding a question into a complex sentence (who... / how many people...).
Expressing a desire for someone to do something (wanting someone to do something for you).
Relaying information heard from others (heard that..., apparently...).
Apparently, he would also like to be told how many people are coming and which countries they are from.
default.tests.0.skills.2.sections.1.passages.0.s: Used to name or identify: a person/thing named or called... (a man named Yamamoto)
I heard that..., reportedly... (relaying information heard from others)
I heard that a man named Mr. Yamamoto found a wallet near a convenience store.
Someone does something for the speaker (calling the school for me)
Used to explain or recount a situation with emphasis
And then, after seeing my student ID card, he called the school for me.
call, phone, make a phone call
To promise/arrange to do something (arranged to meet Mr. Yamamoto)
That evening, I arranged to meet Mr. Yamamoto in front of the convenience store.
Looks like..., seems... (judgment based on appearance: a kind-looking person)
Mr. Yamamoto was a kind-looking person.
Embedded question in a sentence: whether... or not
Try doing something (try looking / checking inside)
Then, he handed me the wallet and said, "Please check inside to see if everything is still there."
to be inside, to be contained
please take a look, please try looking
Both the money and the cards were completely intact.
I expressed my gratitude, saying, "Thank you very much."
thank you, thank you very much
Listing actions in sequential order: connects actions occurring one after another
To become... (expresses a change of state: became warm)
When I returned home and looked at my wallet, I remembered Mr. Yamamoto's face and felt a warm feeling inside.
If / When... (hypothetical condition: if picked up)
To think that... (expresses one's thoughts or feelings)
I also thought that if I picked up someone's lost item, (          ).
Doing V2 after doing V1 (emphasizes chronological sequence: returning home after buying food)
Late at night three days ago, after buying some food at a convenience store, I went home.
Connecting consecutive actions in chronological order (arriving home, then opening the bag)
When I arrived home and opened my bag, I was startled.
Used to explain the reason or background of a situation (explains why the speaker was startled in the previous sentence)
was not there, did not exist, was missing
Conjunction connecting two clauses with contrast or concession (although..., but...)
Expresses an ongoing state of an object (the items remaining inside the wallet)
Although it was a cheap wallet, inside were various cards and my part-time job earnings.
Hypothetical conditional pattern: 'if... then...' (if lost, it would be troublesome)
All of them are things that would cause a lot of trouble if lost.
every one, all of them, any
to be troubled, to be in distress, to have difficulty
Doing an action together with someone (together with a friend)
Conjunction expressing contrast (searched, but could not find it)
I left home right away and searched for my wallet with a friend, but could not find it.
could not find, was not found
To consult, discuss, or seek advice from someone (here, a teacher)
Conjunction expressing contrast (went to the police box, but it was still no use)
The next day, I consulted my teacher at school and went to the police box near my house, but as expected, it was no use.
was no good, was unsuccessful, failed
Indicates the time an event occurs (when / while crying)
Indicates an action directed toward the speaker (a call coming from the school to me)
When I was crying with sadness, a phone call came in from my teacher.
default.tests.1.skills.2.sections.0.passages.0.s: Whenever..., when... (indicates a natural consequence or inevitable occurrence; here, describes what happens when spring arrives)
Called..., known as... (used to define or name something)
Come to..., reach the point where... (expresses a change in state or condition over time)
Although onions are displayed in stores during every season, when spring arrives, ones called "new onions" can be seen.
to be seen, to be found, can be seen
to be lined up, to be on display, to be on sale
fresh onion, early-harvest onion, spring onion
Used to emphasize information or provide an explanation / background context
The harvest time is the same, but what happens afterwards is different.
Only after doing... (indicates chronological sequence of actions)
Passive voice (in this sentence, indicates that onions 'are sold')
Regular onions are sold only after the outer layer dries and turns brown, but fresh onions are sold immediately.
fresh onion, early-harvest onion, spring onion
Both... and... (used to list multiple items sharing the same characteristic)
Both the taste and the texture when eating are slightly different.
Because / since... (expresses an objective reason or cause)
Even if... / Even though... (tastes good even when eaten raw)
Can do something (expresses the ability or possibility to perform an action)
Because fresh onions are sweet and tender, they can be eaten raw and still taste delicious.
fresh onion, early-harvest onion, spring onion
can do, to be able to
Only... (indicates exclusivity, unique to fresh onions)
Please be sure to experience the unique deliciousness found only in fresh onions, quite different from ordinary onions.
spring onion, fresh onion, new onion
please try to feel, please experience
default.tests.1.skills.2.sections.0.passages.1.s: Particle indicating the cause, reason, or purpose of an action (e.g., traveling for work).
My older brother often travels to regional areas for work.
Expresses a situation or outcome decided by external circumstances (ending up having to stay overnight).
Sentence pattern expressing purpose: so that an action can be performed (so that he can leave at any time).
Expresses a continuing state resulting from a completed preparatory action (keeping it prepared).
In most cases, he ends up staying overnight at his destination, so he always keeps an "overnight bag" ready so that he can leave at any time.
can go, to be able to go
Non-exhaustive listing of representative nouns (such as N1, N2, etc.).
Expresses purpose used together with an evaluative adjective (necessary for staying overnight).
Inside it, he keeps items needed for staying overnight, such as underwear and glasses.
Conjunction connecting two clauses with a mild contrast (convenient, but...).
Expresses obligation or necessity: must do, have to do (must pay attention, be careful).
Expresses the existence of a certain matter or point (there is something one must be careful about).
However, while the "overnight bag" is convenient, there is something one must be careful about.
must be careful, have to watch out
to exist, to have, to be
Expresses an unintended action with a sense of regret (ended up mistaking).
Used at the end of a sentence to explain or clarify the preceding subject (It is that...).
That is mistakenly confusing it with one's everyday work bag.
Indicates a specific item out of two options being compared or distinguished (the one containing items).
Expresses an unintended or careless action (ended up taking it).
Conveys hearsay or reported information (I heard that..., apparently...).
I heard that the other day, he also accidentally brought the one containing clothes to work.
contained inside, inside, to be put in
to take along, to carry away
Acknowledges and understands the preceding point, but introduces a counterargument afterward (I understand that..., but...).
Indicates a choice or decision (to decide on, to make it the same).
Advises that one should do something (here as やめたほうがいい: should stop / had better avoid doing).
I understand that he likes it, but I think it would be better not to choose the exact same color and shape as his everyday work bag.
to like, to be fond of
default.tests.1.skills.2.sections.0.passages.2.s: N2 from / sent from N1 (noun modifying another noun using particle から).
This is a postcard from a friend.
Particle indicating the recipient of a letter or postcard (To..., Dear...).
It has been a long time since we last spoke.
long time no see, after a long time
Used with na-adjectives (元気に) to indicate maintaining a state of health or routine (staying healthy)
To start performing an action (住みはじめて: started living)
A period of time passes (１か月がたちました: one month has passed)
One month has passed since I started living in Okinawa.
To get used to / adapt to something (生活に慣れて)
Expresses a habit or repeated action in the present (泳いでいます)
I have also gotten used to life here, and on weekends I often swim in the beautiful sea.
Way of doing something / how to do (作り方: how to make; 弾き方: how to play)
To be taught by someone, to learn from someone
Recently, a neighbor taught me how to make Okinawan dishes (next time, I will also learn how to play an Okinawan musical instrument!).
how to make, way of making
how to play (an instrument), way of playing
Due to / for reasons related to N (expresses an objective cause or reason)
It is decided that / end up having to do due to external circumstances rather than purely personal choice (来ることになって)
Due to work, I suddenly had to move here, and at first I was worried about various things, but now I am really enjoying life here.
To come in order to do something (expresses the purpose of movement: 遊びに来る - come to hang out/visit)
Please definitely / by all means do something (warm, earnest invitation)
Please be sure to come visit during summer vacation.
Month 〇, Day 〇 — Takako Hayashi
default.tests.1.skills.2.sections.1.passages.0.s: Past-tense noun-modifying clause modifying a noun (the essay that Marie wrote).
This is an essay written by Marie.
Expresses an ongoing thought or belief that formed previously and continues into the present (to think that / to consider as...).
The particle も expresses similarity or inclusion (even Yu-san...).
Therefore, now, I think of ①Yu-san as my grandmother as well.
Expresses that something occurred in the past (there were times when...).
Used for hearsay to convey information heard from others (I heard that..., apparently...).
I heard that even someone like Yu had times when she was feeling down.
not well, feeling down, lacking energy
heard that there was, apparently existed
Specifies the point in time after an action or event has completed (when/at the time that...).
That was when her husband passed away.
Unable to bring oneself to do something / not in the mood to do something.
Expresses doing nothing but a certain action repeatedly (doing nothing but looking at the garden).
Hearsay reporting: indicates relaying information heard from others (I heard that...).
Reportedly, she could not bring herself to do anything, spending every day just staring at the garden.
could not bring oneself to, unable to feel like
was looking at, was watching, was gazing at
Noticing an ongoing action or state (uses の to nominalize the clause before the particle に).
However, one day, she noticed that the cherry blossoms in the garden were blooming.
Defines or specifies the content of the following noun (a message saying that...).
It won't do to... / You shouldn't... (used to warn or advise that something is unacceptable).
I heard that (they) thought... (combines thought と思う and hearsay そうだ).
Cherry blossoms were her husband's favorite flowers, and Yu reportedly felt it was a message from him saying, "You can't go on like this."
as it is, like this, this way
Used to explain or define the meaning of a word or phrase (means...).
I heard that... (hearsay; conveying information received from others).
I heard that the "Yu" in Ms. Yu's name means kind and gentle.
the kanji 優 in a name
To come to a place for the purpose of doing something (coming to chat).
Neighbors often come over to Ms. Yu's house to chat.
come to talk, come to chat
Expresses performing an action and then moving away from the speaker's location (heading home).
And then, everyone always leaves with a bright smile.
Causative form (here 'そうさせている' means 'making/causing them to become like that').
Used to emphasize a reason or provide an explanation for what was just mentioned.
Sentence pattern used to express one's thoughts, opinions, or conjectures ('I think that...').
I think it must be Ms. Yu's warm heart that makes them that way.
Used to explain or specify the subject/referent being talked about ('referring to...').
(Note 1) Husband: in this sentence, refers to Ms. Yu's husband.
Te-form used to describe a state or the manner of performing an action
(Note 2) Smiling: smiling (with a calm, cheerful face).
Polite negative form of a noun predicate (is not...).
However, she is not my real grandmother.
Expresses an ongoing state of living/residing in the present (living in...).
Ms. Yuu lives alone in the house next door.
Expresses someone doing something as a favor for the speaker with gratitude (spoke to me).
On the way back from somewhere or after an activity (on the way home from school).
Exactly one year ago, on my way home from school, Ms. Yuu spoke to me.
way back, returning home, after school
calling out to, striking up a conversation
Negative form of desire (do not want to do something).
Expresses a feeling or thought that continued over a period of time in the past.
I had a fight with a friend at school, and I was thinking that I didn't want to go to school anymore.
Expresses someone doing an action as a favor for the speaker (she kindly listened to me).
Expresses a change in feelings or mood (to come to feel like going to school).
However, Yu-san quietly listened to me, saying, "That must have been tough," and before long, I felt like going to school again.
To make someone or something become a certain state (na-adjective + にする: to cheer someone up / make someone feel energetic).
Past-tense noun-modifying clause (the grandmother who passed away).
My late biological grandmother also quietly listened to me and cheered me up.
listening to what someone says, listening
cheered me up, made me feel better
default.tests.2.skills.2.sections.0.passages.0.s: Clause modifying the following noun 「メール」 (the email that Yoko sent)
This is an email that Yoko sent to Mikiko.
Only after doing V... (emphasizes waiting until recovering before making plans).
It is completely fine to wait until after you feel better.
Potential form of the verb 「来る」 (来られる: can come -> 来られない: cannot come)
Expresses a change of state: 'to become unable to do something' or 'to no longer do something'
It was such a pity that you couldn't make it to the party last week.
became unable to come, couldn't make it
Phrase expressing one's physical condition or health
Past continuous form indicating a sustained state in the past
Sentence-ending particle providing new information to the listener
Mr. Tanaka was worried about you as well.
Polite invitation pattern ('Would you like to...?' / 'Shall we...?')
Particle 「で」 indicating scope or the number of people performing an action together
So, why don't the three of us meet up with Mr. Tanaka next time?
as three people, the three of us
won't you meet?, shall we meet?
Quotes a third party's statement ('said that...')
Conjunction indicating an objective cause or reason ('because...', 'since...')
Suggests a representative example ('...or something, for example')
Mr. Tanaka mentioned that he found a lovely café, so let's have a meal or something there.
Please let me know which day works for you, Mikiko.
please tell, please let me know
Indicates someone doing a favor or action for the speaker ('do for me/us')
Mr. Tanaka will make a reservation at the cafe for us, so I will let him know.
Polite request or advice not to do something ('please don't...')
Please don't push yourself too hard.
default.tests.2.skills.2.sections.0.passages.1.s: Pattern expressing a liking or preference for something (N が好きです).
Used to emphasize a large quantity (drinking many cups).
Every day, I drink several cups.
Te-form used to connect actions in chronological sequence (waking up, then drinking right away).
First, I drink it right after waking up in the morning.
first, first of all, to begin with
Doing the subsequent action without doing the preceding action (drinking without putting anything in).
In the morning, I drink it without adding anything.
Conjunction connecting two clauses to express contrast (although..., but...).
Volitional form used for self-talk or expressing personal determination (let's do our best).
Noun-modifying phrasing used to define or explain the content of the following noun (the feeling/thought that...).
Although it is bitter, it wakes me up and puts me in the mood to do my best all day today.
let's do our best, let's work hard
Expresses two actions occurring simultaneously (drinking while eating sweets).
In the afternoon, around 3 o'clock, I drink it while eating sweets.
Uses the particle は to compare and contrast two opposing situations (in summer..., in winter...).
In the summer, I drink cold coffee, and in the winter, I drink hot coffee.
Indicates a reason or cause (because the sweets are sweet...).
Because the sweets are sweet, I drink it just as it is.
Uses the te-form to connect two sequential actions (adding milk and then drinking).
In the evening, I add plenty of milk and drink it.
Expresses two actions occurring simultaneously (listening to music while drinking).
Conditional pattern indicating a natural or inevitable consequence (whenever/if you do..., you feel...).
Potential form expressing the ability to do something (able to relax).
When I drink it while listening to my favorite music, I can relax and feel very refreshed.
default.tests.2.skills.2.sections.0.passages.2.s: The particle と indicates a companion performing an action together (with someone), combined with the structure N に行く (go to do activity N).
On Sunday, I went cherry blossom viewing with my friends.
Nominalizes a verb using の (seeing cherry blossoms... was the first time).
It was my first time seeing cherry blossoms.
to see, to watch, to look at
for the first time, first time
Expresses two actions occurring simultaneously (eating boxed lunches while viewing cherry blossoms).
The particle で indicates the state or number of participants performing an action (doing something together).
We ate boxed lunches together while viewing the cherry blossoms.
The te-form of an i-adjective used to connect two clauses or list attributes (the weather is nice AND the flowers are beautiful).
The weather was nice too, and the cherry blossoms were very beautiful.
good, nice (te-form of いい/よい)
Indicates a conjecture based on visual appearance ('looks like...', 'seems...'). Note that いい/よい changes to よさそう
Noun-modifying clause (people who are present / who have come to view the flowers)
Moreover, the people who came to view the cherry blossoms all seemed to get along well and looked like they were having fun.
seeming on good terms, appearing close
seemed fun, looked like they were having a good time
Uses the conjectural form そうだ in noun-modifying form ('people who look happy')
Indicates a change of state or mood ('became cheerful')
Seeing so many happy-looking people, I also felt very cheerful.
default.tests.2.skills.2.sections.1.passages.0.s: To start doing an action (verb stem without ます + はじめる)
Recently, I started learning to play the piano.
Transitioning to a new state or age (turning 60 years old)
Used to explain the background context or reason
Last year, when I turned 60 and retired from work, I had free time.
Written negative form of "〜ないで", meaning "without doing V" (まちがわずに: without making mistakes).
Indicates comparison, meaning "rather than... / instead of..." (まちがわずにひくことより: rather than playing without mistakes).
Expresses someone doing something for oneself with gratitude (教えてくれます: kindly teaches me).
However, now, rather than just playing without making mistakes, my teacher teaches me how to play.
without making a mistake, without error
Expresses trying to do something (ひいてみましょう: let's try playing).
Used to list representative examples in an illustrative way ("things like... and...", "such as...").
Indicates the topic or object of thought or discussion (曲のイメージについて: about the image/feeling of the piece).
My teacher talks to me about the imagery of the piece, saying things like, "Let's try playing gently at the beginning," or "From here, the feeling of joy grows bigger and bigger."
Indicates transforming or turning something into something else (イメージを音にする: turn imagery into sound).
Conjugation of an い-adjective indicating a change of state (楽しくなった: became fun/more enjoyable).
Sentence-ending expression used to explain a reason or express personal feelings in a natural, friendly tone.
And so, I also began to find it enjoyable to turn my own images into sound.
and so, therefore, because of that
to make, to turn into, to do
Pluralizing suffix attached to nouns referring to people (生徒たち: students).
Indicates the time an event or activity takes place (10月に...発表会があります: there is a recital in October).
Every year in October, there is a recital with the teacher and the students.
to be held, to take place, there is
Expresses the speaker's own desire (出たい: want to participate).
Expresses an intention or ongoing thought that the speaker has held over time ("I am thinking of... / I intend to...").
I am thinking that I would like to participate in this year's recital too.
want to participate, want to perform
Conjunction connecting two clauses with a contrasting or concessive meaning ("although..., but...").
Used to connect actions in chronological sequence ("practice a lot, and then...").
I am still not very good, but I will practice a lot and (do my best...).
Continuously maintaining an action (verb stem without ます + 続ける)
Change of state (i-adjective drop い + くなる: to become...)
Expresses regret or remorse over an action that unintentionally occurred
I had been taking piano lessons since childhood, but during high school my studies became busy and I ended up quitting.
Ever since doing something, a new state begins and continues
To reach a state of no longer doing something (drop い from V-ない + くなる)
Ever since I started working, I had so much overtime that I stopped thinking about the piano.
Intended for or aimed at someone/something (N + のための + N)
Expresses a resulting state already in place (the flyer was already inside the newspaper)
However, about six months after quitting my job, one day there was a flyer for adult piano lessons tucked inside the newspaper.
to quit, to leave, to stop
Nominalizes a clause to refer to an action or fact (the fact that I used to learn piano)
Seeing that, I remembered that I used to take piano lessons.
to see, to look, to watch
was learning, used to take lessons
To come to want to do something (drop い from V-たい + くなる: spontaneous desire)
Because of that, I wanted to try playing again.
and so, therefore, because of that
Different from... (used to indicate a contrast or difference).
Suffix that transforms an い-adjective into a noun indicating degree or quality (楽しい -> 楽しさ).
Taking piano lessons again after a long time, I discovered a different kind of joy from when I was a child.
after a long time, for the first time in a while
to differ, to be different, to vary
Just as..., exactly according to... (following existing instructions or content).
Expresses a resulting state from an intentional action (it has already been written on the sheet music).
In order to..., so as to... (V-ない + ように: so as not to make a mistake).
When I was a child, I used to play just as written on the sheet music, making sure not to make any mistakes.
to not make a mistake, to not go wrong
When / whenever... (conditional indicating a natural consequence or habitual reaction).
Lists clauses and adds supporting reasons or points (and, not only... but also...).
Passive voice (to have an action done by someone: 先生にほめられる - to be praised by the teacher).
When I was able to play correctly and skillfully, I was happy, and my teacher praised me as well.
was glad, was happy, was delighted
